# Components

Everything a config can name with `type:`, slot by slot. The page is generated from
the registries, from what each class declares about itself and from the shipped
configs, so it shows what is in the code, not what was planned. The same tables in
a terminal:

```bash
grasppanda components                    # every slot
grasppanda components --slot backbones   # one slot, with the meaning of its columns
grasppanda components PTv3               # one component: options, configs, what it fits
grasppanda components --json             # for scripts
```

Which components can replace which, and what a swap changes besides the line in the
config, is the subject of [Swapping components](advanced_guides/swapping.md). Turning a
combination into a checked config and trying it on real frames is
[Try a combination](user_guides/combinations.md); what that gave for every component
under every method is [Measured combinations](advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md).

## How to read the tables

- **Contract columns** (between the name and the status) are the class attributes the
  config checker compares before anything is built. Each slot explains its own.
- **Status** is what has been proven. `tested`: unit tests on CPU cover the
  component's contract and behaviour; for the stages of a ported method, the method's
  page under [Model zoo](model_zoo.md) says how it was compared with the reference
  implementation. `weights-verified`: additionally, weights released by the authors
  load strictly and the outputs match the official implementation; the measured
  difference is on the [scene encoder page](model_zoo_backbones.md). `bridge`: the
  component is an adapter around a library installed as an optional extra; the
  library's own code runs, and the tests here cover the adapter (contract, shapes,
  gradients), not the library. `—`: the class declares no status. No status is a
  claim about grasp-detection accuracy.
- **Source** is the paper, method or library the component implements, and where the
  code comes from: written for GraspPanda from the paper and the behaviour of the
  reference code (the ported grasp methods; licences and commits of the references
  are in the method READMEs), a bridge to a library, or adapted from permissively
  licensed code (listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`).
- **Needs** lists optional dependencies (`pip install -e ".[...]"`).
- **Shipped configs** are the runnable configs under `configs/` whose resolved tree
  names the component.

## Detectors

`model` — A complete method. Seed-based detectors fill the six slots below.

- `required_inputs`: Observation fields the detector reads; the dataset must provide them.
- `needs_supervision`: Fields of the training supervision the component reads (`objects` are the dense label grids), each with the option that makes it read the field. The training dataset must serve every one; the config check compares.

## Seed proposals

`model.proposal` — Scene features to seeds.

- `requires`: The kind of scene features the proposal works on (`dense`, `subsampled`, `any`).
- `seed_scores`: Per-seed scores the stage predicts, supervises and stores on the seeds. A score has one owner per detector.
- `needs_supervision`: Fields of the training supervision the component reads (`objects` are the dense label grids), each with the option that makes it read the field. The training dataset must serve every one; the config check compares.

## View stages

`model.view` — One approach direction per seed.

- `seed_scores`: Per-seed scores the stage predicts, supervises and stores on the seeds. A score has one owner per detector.
- `label_formats`: Kinds of matched labels the view stage can compute its targets from.
- `needs_matched`: Optional fields of the matched labels the stage cannot work without; the assigner must return them.
- `applies_seed_weights`: Whether the losses honour a per-seed weight from the assigner. An assigner that returns weights is refused next to a stage that would ignore them.

## Assigners

`model.assigner` — Training only: seeds and chosen views to matched grasp labels.

- `label_format`: Kind of matched labels: `dense` (angle × depth grids per view) or `compact` (one grasp per point and view). Assigner and head bundle must agree.
- `optional_outputs`: Optional fields of the matched labels the assigner can return, each with the option that switches it on.
- `needs_supervision`: Fields of the training supervision the component reads (`objects` are the dense label grids), each with the option that makes it read the field. The training dataset must serve every one; the config check compares.

- `out_axes`: Named axes of the crop features. Must equal the head bundle's `in_axes`.

## Head bundles

`model.head` — Head bundle: prediction layers, target encoder, loss and decoder as one unit.

- `in_axes`: Named axes of the crop features the head bundle expects.
- `label_format`: Kind of matched labels: `dense` (angle × depth grids per view) or `compact` (one grasp per point and view). Assigner and head bundle must agree.
- `score_kind`: Meaning of the decoded grasp score. Scores of different kinds are not comparable.
- `applies_seed_weights`: Whether the losses honour a per-seed weight from the assigner. An assigner that returns weights is refused next to a stage that would ignore them.
- `needs_supervision`: Fields of the training supervision the component reads (`objects` are the dense label grids), each with the option that makes it read the field. The training dataset must serve every one; the config check compares.

## Primitive losses

`<stage>.<name>_loss` — Primitive loss inside a stage.

- `accepts`: Kinds of loss term the primitive fits: `class` (logits against class indices), `unit` (a target quality in [0, 1]), `value` (an unbounded target) or `bins` (logits against a fractional bin position). A stage names the kind of each of its loss options, and the config check refuses any other pairing.
- `prediction`: How the primitive reads the output of a `unit` term: as the `value` itself or as a `logit`. A stage hands a logit on through its sigmoid.

## Hooks

`hooks[i]` — Extra behaviour around the training loop.

| Component | Status | Source | What it is | Needs | Shipped configs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AdaptiveGradClipHook` | `bridge` | Brock et al. (arXiv 2102.06171), via timm.utils.adaptive_clip_grad | Adaptive gradient clipping: bound each unit's gradient by a fraction of its weight norm. | `optim` | — |
| `BNMomentumHook` | — | BN momentum schedule of the PointNet++-based methods | Decays the momentum of every batch-norm layer in steps of epochs. | — | `experimental/graspnet-baseline_sunet14-fps_g1b-realsense_18e`<br>`graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense-to-gc6d-d435_18e`<br>`graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e`<br>`hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-kinect_15e`<br>`hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense-to-gc6d-d435_15e`<br>`hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e`<br>`scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense-to-gc6d-d435_18e`<br>`scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e` |
| `CheckpointHook` | — | GraspPanda | Writes `checkpoints/epoch_NNNN.pth` and `checkpoints/best.pth`. | — | — |
| `EMAHook` | `tested` | Tarvainen and Valpola, NeurIPS 2017 (arXiv 1703.01780), via torch.optim.swa_utils | Exponential moving average of the weights, with warm-up of the decay. | — | — |
| `EpochSignalHook` | — | GraspPanda | Calls `model.on_train_epoch(epoch, max_epochs)` before every epoch. | — | `hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-kinect_15e`<br>`hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense-to-gc6d-d435_15e`<br>`hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e` |
| `EvaluationHook` | — | GraspPanda | Predicts on `data.val` and scores every variant of `evaluation.variants`. | — | — |
| `FreezeHook` | `tested` | Howard and Ruder, ACL 2018 (arXiv 1801.06146): gradual unfreezing | Freeze sub-modules for the first epochs (or for the whole run), then release them. | — | — |
| `SWAHook` | `tested` | Izmailov et al., UAI 2018 (arXiv 1803.05407), via torch.optim.swa_utils | Stochastic weight averaging: the equal-weight mean of the weights after late epochs. | — | — |
| `ScheduleFreeHook` | `tested` | Defazio et al., The Road Less Scheduled (arXiv 2405.15682), via schedulefree | Switch a schedule-free optimizer between its training point and its average. | — | — |
| `StageTimerHook` | — | GraspPanda | Times the forward pass of each stage (direct child module) of the detector. | — | — |
| `TensorBoardLoggerHook` | — | GraspPanda | Writes scalars to `<run dir>/tensorboard`: `train/*` by iteration, `eval/*` by epoch. | `tensorboard` | — |
| `TextLoggerHook` | — | GraspPanda | Prints one line per interval to the console and to `log.txt`. | — | — |
| `WandbLoggerHook` | — | GraspPanda | Logs scalars to Weights & Biases; the run is named after the run directory. | `wandb` | — |

## Optimizers

`optimizer` — Every optimizer of torch.optim, by its class name.

Named by class, whatever the installed PyTorch provides; `grasppanda components --slot optimizers` lists them.

| Component | Status | Source | What it is | Needs | Shipped configs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ParamGroups` | `tested` | Bao et al., BEiT (arXiv 2106.08254): layer-wise decay as in timm.optim | Parameter groups for any optimizer: per-module rates, layer-wise decay, no decay on 1-D. | — | — |
| `PytorchOptimizer` | `bridge` | Kim, pytorch_optimizer (kozistr/pytorch_optimizer), via the library | Any optimizer of pytorch_optimizer by its name (`prodigy`, `ademamix`, `soap`, …). | `optim` | — |
| `ScheduleFree` | `bridge` | Defazio et al., The Road Less Scheduled (arXiv 2405.15682), via schedulefree | A schedule-free optimizer: no learning-rate schedule, the iterates are averaged instead. | `optim` | — |
| `TimmOptimizer` | `bridge` | Wightman, PyTorch Image Models (timm.optim), via timm | Any optimizer of timm by its name (`lamb`, `adan`, `adopt`, `lion`, `mars`, …). | `optim` | — |

## Schedulers

`scheduler` — Every scheduler of torch.optim.lr_scheduler, by its class name.

Named by class, whatever the installed PyTorch provides; `grasppanda components --slot schedulers` lists them.

| Component | Status | Source | What it is | Needs | Shipped configs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TimmSchedule` | `bridge` | Wightman, PyTorch Image Models (timm.scheduler), via timm | A schedule of `timm.scheduler` by name: cosine, tanh, polynomial, step, multi-step. | `optim` | — |
| `WarmupCosineLR` | `tested` | FineGrasp (arXiv 2507.05978) | Linear warm-up, then a cosine: the schedule of the FineGrasp reference. | — | `finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e` |
